label: Cause of esse versus sufficient reason of existence
term: cause of esse versus sufficient reason of existence
resolution: In ST I q.3 a.4's first proof the two forks are about *causing* the subject's esse: sufficient efficient causation by the subject's essential principles alone versus causation by an exterior agent. The no-self-cause premise excludes the former *causal* fork only. A noncausal essential truth, global ground, or primitive fact is not a third kind of efficient cause by definition; admitting such alternatives challenges the exhaustiveness of the causal dichotomy. Leibniz's sufficient-reason demand in Monadology §§32–38 is a separately sourced explanatory proposal and is not silently substituted for Aquinas' efficient cause. No claim about metaphysical possibility follows from a finite mathematical countermodel. Declaration-completion audit (2026-11-09): sense 1 currently has only the primitive Profile.essentialPrinciplesAloneSufficeForEsse field, not a definition of essential efficient sufficiency. Replacing it by self-CausesIn would add an unproved identification between a being as agent and its essential principles as sufficient source; wrapping the field would leave the same semantic gap. Sense 3 points to the Leibnizian whole-contingent-series definition, not a generic noncausal explanation of one individual. Neither the absence of efficient causation nor a free reason flag defines explanatory adequacy, and the existing series definition does not itself require noncausality. OPEN for coordinator: retain the series-level sense and define its explanandum/reason/adequacy/outside-series vocabulary, or introduce a separate analyst individual noncausal sense with explicit bridges; do not silently replace the existing sense. Both missing declarations and their legacy allowances remain unfinished. Causal exhaustiveness and the no-self-cause premise remain open.
